artworks.title: Chaos
artworks.description: A visionary oil painting from Watts's allegorical cycle 'The House of Life', imagining the primordial state before order: titanic elemental figures heave out of fire and vapour as the world struggles into being. This version, executed by Watts with his studio assistants, is held by Tate, London.

artworks.title: Chaos
artworks.description: A panel from the Ciudad Rodrigo altarpiece imagines the primordial void before creation — Chaos as swirling disorder from which the ordered world will emerge, now in the University of Arizona Museum of Art.

artworks.title: The Creation of the World (Orbis fabrica)
artworks.description: Tempesta's Met etching for Ovid opens with the world drawn out of formless Chaos — earth, sea, and sky separating as the first metamorphosis of all.

popCulture.title: Chaos (cosmogony)
popCulture.description: Hesiod's first gap endures as cosmogony's opening word — Chaos as the void before Earth, from which later ages borrowed disorder.

popCulture.title: Chaos
popCulture.description: English chaos names utter disorder — the primordial deity reduced to the ordinary word for a mess.
